ranked_evidence.title: Ebola death toll in DR Congo surpasses 1,000 - NPR
ranked_evidence.snippet: **DR Congo Ebola Death Toll Tops 1,000 as Outbreak Accelerates** **Congo's Ebola outbreak has crossed the grim 1,000-death threshold, marking the fastest fatal surge in recorded history of the virus.**. # Ebola death toll in DR Congo surpasses 1,000. #### Over 1,000 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak. KINSHASA, Democratic Republic of Congo—More than 1,000 people have died of Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to official figures released Thursday, with the outbreak showing no sign of slowing. Funding is also a problem, as the severely degraded local health system in eastern Congo, as well as NGOs, struggles to cope as Ebola spreads in remote rural areas. In mid-July, the WHO said its joint $518 million plan to fight the disease, with the Africa Centers for Disease Control, faced a funding shortfall of over $400 million. According to official figures, four people have died of Ebola in its capital Kisangani, a major trading center of over 1 million people, with direct links to Congo's capital Kinshasa.

ranked_evidence.title: Why No Brit Or European Can Ignore August’s Total Solar Eclipse - Forbes
ranked_evidence.snippet: Europe’s biggest skywatching event of 2026 arrives on Aug. 12, when a total solar eclipse crosses Greenland, Iceland and Spain. To experience a total solar eclipse, you *must* be within its narrow path of totality. However, millions outside the path of totality will still see a deep partial eclipse, including a rare eclipsed sunset across much of central and eastern Europe. For many, it will be the deepest solar eclipse since 1999 — and it occurs on the same day as the peak of the annual Perseid meteor shower. Aug. 12’s total solar eclipse will be the first since 2015 and the first visible from mainland Europe since 1999, but it will only be visible from a narrow 180-mile (290-kilometer) path of totality through eastern Greenland, western Iceland and northern Spain. To experience totality — a brief opportunity to see the sun’s beautiful corona with the naked eye — you must be inside the path of totality.

ranked_evidence.title: Ebola Deaths Surpass 1,000 in Congo as Virus Outpaces Response - Bloomberg Law News
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Ebola Deaths Surpass 1,000 in Congo as Virus Outpaces Response. Confirmed Ebola deaths in Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed 1,000, prompting Africa’s top public health official to warn the outbreak could become one of the worst on record unless transmission is rapidly brought under control. The number of fatal cases has doubled in just over two weeks, with the National Institute of Public Health reporting 2,536 cases and 1,033 deaths on Thursday. The death toll has climbed from 506 on July 4, with the epidemic spreading into two new provinces beyond its original epicenter in Ituri. ranked_evidence.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak has killed more than 1,000 people - Los Angeles Times
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Congo’s Ebola outbreak has killed more than 1,000 people. BUNIA, Congo — More than 1,000 people have died in the Ebola outbreak in Congo, according to Africa’s top health body, a grim toll as conflict, community resistance and an uneven response fuel its spread. Speaking at a health summit in Ghana on Wednesday, Dr. Jean Kaseya, director-general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, said 1,031 deaths have been confirmed in the fastest Ebola outbreak in history. It has also killed more people at a faster rate than any outbreak on record, including the 2013-2016 outbreak that is considered the worst — with over 11,000 deaths out of at least 28,000 cases. Officials have warned that 80% of new cases have emerged outside known chains of transmission, a sign the outbreak is spreading faster than health officials can track it even as they step up their response in Ituri province, the epicenter of the outbreak, and four other provinces where cases have been recorded.

ranked_evidence.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed nearly 1,000 people - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed nearly 1,000 people. At least 999 people have died from the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo, according to official data published overnight into Wednesday, a grim toll in what’s already been declared the fastest Ebola outbreak in history. BUNIA, Congo -- At least 999 people have died from the Ebola outbreak in Congo, according to official data published overnight into Wednesday, a grim toll in what’s already been declared the fastest Ebola outbreak in history. The latest update from Congo’s Ministry of Health shows that as of Monday, 2,473 cases have been recorded in the latest outbreak, and 999 people have died. It has also killed more people at a quicker rate than any outbreak on record, including the 2013-2016 outbreak that is considered the worst on record with over 11,000 deaths out of at least 28,000 cases.
